items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: I had Tom and Teddoh playing with me.

ctx.x: I wanted to ask you, did Tom Brown play with you? Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. He's one of the two Teddors. I had Tom and Teddoh playing with me. Yeah. I had five bands Johnny going all the time. Steve Brown played with you too, huh? That's Ted. That's his name. Who? Ted, huh? Ted. Ted. They called him Steve later on. Yeah. Teddoh. Yeah. Teddoh. Uh-huh. Yeah. They called him Steve. Yeah. He was in town recently too. Yeah, I know. I met him. He looked me up. Yeah. He's a wonderful bass player.
There's Merritt. He's good bass player. He's right here. Merritt.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine Interview, 1960-05-23
items.q: I believe Tom Brown was a man who went up north first. I think he did, too. ... we used to speak about these things, you know.

ctx.x: Yes. And, uh, of course, it happened to be close to a Mardi Gras. And I had three bands out that year. And, uh, well, little Brunus, Abby, he was a pretty fair corner player. It was then at that time, too. He was picking up mighty nice, very nice. Well, he sends Abby Brunus in each place to play that carnival parade. While he went around scouting, I guess, to get members to go north with, see? Now, he claims he went first there, to went up north first. No. I believe Tom Brown was a man who went up north first. I…
I believe he went a year before or so.

items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine and Alfred Laine Interview, 1951-04-21
items.q: I picked them boys up playing with me when they were just small children.

ctx.x: I sure did, lots of them.
I see. Now, another thing, too. Do you remember Tom Brown and Harry Shields when they used to play in the old days?
Yes, I do remember. I picked them boys up playing with me when they were just small children.
